newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian refinery still hopes for Merrill loan.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian refinery still hopes for Merrill loan.

text.p: Lithuania's troubled Mazheikiu Nafta refinery said it still hoped for a $19 million loan from Merrill Lynch although the government has rejected it.
The government earlier issued a guarantee for the credit on the condition it was priced at 0.75 basis points over Libor with conditions tied to movements in the price of oil.
But it rejected new Merrill Lynch conditions, which raised the interest rate to Libor +2 basis points with no link to the oil price.
"This is a very good offer, I don't see why the government cannot accept it," Mazheikiu Nafta finance department director Vita Petroshiene told Reuters.
The refinery wants the loan to buy oil supplies, as at present it depends on shipments from Russia and often has to close down due to disruptions in the supply.
The funds from Merrill Lynch are intended to pave the way for a larger, $40 million loan the refinery wants from Chase Manhattan without a government guarantee, also for oil purchases.
"We are now negotiating with the finance ministry to take responsiblity for the loan," Petroshiene said.
The refinery made a loss last year of more than 30 million litas and had to shut down for 130 days.
It is to be merged with other parts of the oil sector under one state holding company, Lithuanian Oil.
